markets.name: Harbor Row Market
markets.description: A dockside market known for morning-catch seafood stalls and a long row of cut-flower growers.

markets.name: Old Town Square Market
markets.description: Millhaven's largest and oldest market, held in the square since 1974. Go early for the cheese counter.

markets.name: North Fields Growers Market
markets.description: A grower-only market surrounded by orchards — most stalls are run by the farmers themselves.

markets.name: Riverside Lane Market
markets.description: An after-work weekday market with a strong lineup of bakers and ready-to-eat vendors.

markets.name: South Commons Market
markets.description: A family-friendly Saturday market with a small playground and a weekly live-music slot.

markets.name: East Mill Farmstand Collective
markets.description: A weekend-long indoor collective of year-round farmstands, handy for market visits in bad weather.

produceGuide.name: Asparagus
produceGuide.tip: Look for tight, closed tips and firm stalks.

produceGuide.name: Strawberries
produceGuide.tip: Best flavor comes from berries picked within a day or two.

produceGuide.name: Sweet corn
produceGuide.tip: Buy same-day where possible — sugars fade fast after picking.

produceGuide.name: Tomatoes
produceGuide.tip: Ask growers which variety is ripest that day rather than picking by looks.

produceGuide.name: Zucchini
produceGuide.tip: Smaller squash are more tender than oversized ones.

produceGuide.name: Peaches
produceGuide.tip: A ripe peach smells sweet at the stem end.

produceGuide.name: Apples
produceGuide.tip: Different varieties peak at different weeks — ask what just came in.

produceGuide.name: Winter squash
produceGuide.tip: Cure for a few days at room temperature before storing.

produceGuide.name: Root vegetables
produceGuide.tip: Carrots and parsnips sweeten after the season's first frost.

produceGuide.name: Kale & hardy greens
produceGuide.tip: Cold-weather greens are usually less bitter than summer ones.

produceGuide.name: Citrus
produceGuide.tip: Heavier fruit for its size usually means juicier segments.

produceGuide.name: Mushrooms
produceGuide.tip: Available most of the year from indoor growers — check the stall for what's freshly picked.

spring.label: Spring
spring.blurb: The first tender vegetables of the year are showing up alongside the last of the stored winter roots.

summer.label: Summer
summer.blurb: Peak season — stalls are at their fullest with stone fruit, tomatoes and sweet corn.

autumn.label: Autumn
autumn.blurb: Harvest season for storage crops — a good time to stock up on things that keep.

winter.label: Winter
winter.blurb: A quieter season, led by hardy greens, stored roots and indoor-grown mushrooms.
